hobbies.name: Tennis
hobbies.description: Find your rhythm. One rally at a time.
hobbies.safetyNote: Check the court, warm up gently, keep clear of others and stop if you feel pain.

upgrade.note: Your own graphite racquet, restringing, court shoes, lessons or clinics

gear.name: Racquet
gear.freeAlternative: Many clubs and public courts lend a racquet for a first session.
gear.guidance: Aluminum is fine while you decide if the sport sticks; graphite once it has.

gear.name: Tennis balls
gear.freeAlternative: Whoever you hit with usually has some.
gear.guidance: A fresh can bounces predictably. Old balls are fine for wall practice.

gear.name: Court shoes
gear.freeAlternative: Running shoes work for your first few sessions.
gear.guidance: Court soles grip and protect ankles on lateral moves. Worth it once you play regularly.

gear.name: Hat and sunscreen
gear.guidance: Outdoor courts reflect a lot of sun. Protect yourself before comfort items.

gear.name: Overgrips
gear.guidance: A fresh grip stops the racquet slipping. Add one once the original wears.

hobbies.name: Cycling / Fixed Gear
hobbies.description: A little farther. A little more freedom.
hobbies.safetyNote: Check air, brakes and chain before every ride. Use a fitted helmet and follow local traffic rules. Fixed-gear road use needs a functional front brake; do not learn brakeless street riding.

upgrade.note: Wheels, saddle, clipless pedals and shoes, a drivetrain refresh, a bike fit, tools

gear.name: Helmet
gear.guidance: Buy new and buy for fit. A helmet that has taken one impact is done, even if it looks fine.

gear.name: Bike (fixed or single speed)
gear.freeAlternative: A used track bike, or converting an old steel road frame, is the cheapest honest path.
gear.guidance: Fit and working brakes matter more than weight or looks. Have a shop check a used bike.

gear.name: Front brake
gear.freeAlternative: Included on most complete bikes; about $25–60 to add if yours has none.
gear.guidance: Required for road riding on this path, including fixed gear, whatever your skid skills.

gear.name: U-lock
gear.guidance: A bike without a good lock is a bike on borrowed time. Lock the frame, not just a wheel.

gear.name: Front and rear lights
gear.guidance: Needed from dusk onward and on grey days. Be seen from the front and behind.

gear.name: Multi-tool, pump and spare tube
gear.freeAlternative: Most shops will lend a floor pump.
gear.guidance: Enough to fix a flat by the road. Learn the fix at home first.

hobbies.name: Swimming
hobbies.description: Build confidence, one length at a time.
hobbies.safetyNote: Practice with qualified supervision in a swim-safe environment. Never swim alone, hyperventilate or do breath-holding contests. Restrictive knee bands are not a default freestyle correction.

upgrade.note: Better goggles, a training set, a swim watch, masters club or coached lessons

gear.name: Swimsuit
gear.freeAlternative: Any snug athletic swimwear you already own.
gear.guidance: Anything snug that your pool accepts. Loose clothing drags and can be unsafe.

gear.name: Goggles
gear.guidance: Fit is everything: they should seal lightly without a strap. Not something to share.

gear.name: Pool access
gear.freeAlternative: Campus rec centers and many municipal pools are free or included.
gear.guidance: Choose a pool with lifeguards. Cost varies a lot by area; campus and city pools are often cheapest.

gear.name: Swim cap
gear.guidance: Keeps hair out of your face and the filters. Many pools require one.

gear.name: Towel
gear.freeAlternative: One you own.
gear.guidance: The one you already own is perfect.

gear.name: Fins, pull buoy or kickboard
gear.freeAlternative: Most pools have a shared bin.
gear.guidance: Training tools for later. Ask your instructor before using them.

hobbies.name: PC Building
hobbies.description: Understand the machine, then build it.
hobbies.safetyNote: Unplug at the wall and hold the power button before opening anything. Ground yourself against the bare case or use a strap before touching a board, and never open a power supply — it holds charge long after it is unplugged.

upgrade.note: A faster graphics card, more memory, another drive, a monitor and peripherals

gear.name: CPU
gear.guidance: Match the socket to the motherboard exactly. One generation back is the usual value pick.

gear.name: Motherboard
gear.guidance: Check the socket and memory generation before anything else.

gear.name: Memory (16–32 GB)
gear.guidance: Match the generation the board accepts. Prices are unusually high right now; check before buying.

gear.name: Graphics card
gear.freeAlternative: $0 if your processor has integrated graphics.
gear.guidance: Only needed for games and heavy visual work. A processor with integrated graphics can skip this at first.

gear.name: Storage (1 TB NVMe)
gear.guidance: One solid-state drive is enough to start.

gear.name: Power supply
gear.guidance: Buy this new and leave headroom over what the parts draw. Never the place to cut, and never open one.

gear.name: Case
gear.guidance: Check cooler height and card length against its specification before buying.

gear.name: Operating system
gear.freeAlternative: Linux is free; student licenses often are too.
gear.guidance: Linux is free, and many students can get Windows through their school.

gear.name: #2 Phillips screwdriver
gear.freeAlternative: Almost certainly one in the house already.
gear.guidance: One magnetic screwdriver does the whole build.

gear.name: Anti-static strap
gear.freeAlternative: Touch the bare metal case with the power supply switched off, and avoid carpet.
gear.guidance: Makes it harder to forget to ground yourself.

hobbies.name: Drawing
hobbies.quickStart: Pencil and paper · FREE TO TRY
hobbies.safetyNote: Keep the wrist neutral and draw from the shoulder for large shapes. Take a short break every twenty to thirty minutes, work with light across the page, and stop if your hand aches.

upgrade.note: A quality sketchbook, graphite and charcoal, a drawing board, figure sessions, a tablet

gear.name: Pencil or graphite set
gear.freeAlternative: Any pencil you own.
gear.guidance: Any pencil works. Harder grades smudge less, softer ones shade faster.

gear.name: Paper or sketchbook
gear.freeAlternative: Printer paper, which is what Drawabox itself recommends.
gear.guidance: Cheap paper keeps you from being precious about mistakes, and volume is what teaches.

gear.name: Eraser and sharpener
gear.guidance: A soft eraser lifts graphite without tearing cheap paper.

gear.name: Fineliner pens (0.5 mm)
gear.guidance: Only needed if you follow the Drawabox curriculum, which is drawn in ink.

hobbies.name: Painting
hobbies.description: Mix it, and see what the colour really is.
hobbies.quickStart: Three colours + a brush · LOW COST
hobbies.safetyNote: Work where air moves, keep solvents sealed and away from heat, and never pour them down a drain. Do not eat or point a brush with your mouth. Acrylic and watercolour avoid nearly all of this while you learn.

upgrade.note: Artist-grade paint, stretched canvas, an easel, better brushes, classes

gear.name: Acrylic paint starter set
gear.guidance: Student grade is fine. A red, a blue, a yellow and a white mix almost anything.

gear.name: Brush set
gear.guidance: A few rounds and a flat cover most of what a beginner needs.

gear.name: Painting surface
gear.freeAlternative: Heavy paper or primed cardboard for practice.
gear.guidance: Canvas panels or an acrylic pad. Practice on anything that takes paint.

gear.name: Palette
gear.freeAlternative: A paper plate or plastic lid.
gear.guidance: Anything flat and wipeable. Acrylic peels cleanly off a lid.

gear.name: Water jar and rag
gear.freeAlternative: Any jar and an old shirt.
gear.guidance: Change the water more often than feels necessary.

hobbies.name: Running
hobbies.description: Slower than you think. Further than you expect.
hobbies.safetyNote: Build distance gradually and take a lighter week roughly every fourth. Run facing traffic where there is no path, wear something reflective in low light, plan water in heat, and treat new sharp pain as a reason to stop.

upgrade.note: A second pair for rotation, a GPS watch, race entries, coaching

gear.name: Running shoes
gear.freeAlternative: Any athletic shoe you own will cover your first few weeks; replace it before your mileage builds.
gear.guidance: Fit matters more than model or price. A shop that watches you walk is worth the trip. Not something to buy used.

gear.name: Athletic clothes
gear.freeAlternative: Whatever you already exercise in.
gear.guidance: Whatever you already exercise in.

gear.name: Moisture-wicking socks
gear.guidance: Cotton holds sweat and causes blisters on longer runs.

gear.name: Water bottle
gear.freeAlternative: One you own.
gear.guidance: Needed in heat and on longer runs, or plan a route past water.

gear.name: Reflective vest or headlamp
gear.freeAlternative: Run in daylight.
gear.guidance: Needed for low light, not optional there.

hobbies.name: Volleyball
hobbies.description: Three touches, and everyone is involved.
hobbies.safetyNote: Warm the shoulders, wrists and ankles before hitting. Set with firm fingers, land on two feet, keep out of the space under the net, and call loudly so nobody collides.

upgrade.note: Your own competition ball, court shoes, better pads, league fees

gear.name: Indoor volleyball
gear.freeAlternative: Every gym, rec league and pickup group has balls.
gear.guidance: Sessions almost always provide balls; your own helps solo wall practice.

gear.name: Knee pads
gear.guidance: Cheap, and the floor is unforgiving. Unnecessary on sand.

gear.name: Court shoes
gear.freeAlternative: Any clean non-marking athletic shoe for your first sessions.
gear.guidance: Indoor courts need clean non-marking soles. Court shoes add ankle support for lateral moves.

gear.name: Ankle braces
gear.guidance: Worth considering if you have a history of rolling an ankle.

gear.name: Ball pump
gear.guidance: Only needed once you own a ball.

hobbies.name: Reading
hobbies.quickStart: A library card · FREE TO TRY
hobbies.safetyNote: Read with light on the page rather than behind it, hold the book near eye level, and look at something distant every twenty minutes. Dim screens in the evening and prefer paper near bedtime.

upgrade.note: An e-reader, an audiobook subscription, a book budget, shelves

gear.name: Library card
gear.freeAlternative: Libby gives you ebooks and audiobooks on the same card, from your phone.
gear.guidance: Free at any US public library with proof of address. This is your whole starting kit.

gear.name: A book
gear.freeAlternative: The library, Libby, Project Gutenberg or a Little Free Library.
gear.guidance: Start with something you want to read, not something you think you should.

gear.name: Book light
gear.freeAlternative: Any lamp.
gear.guidance: Light on the page rather than behind it.
